Package neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe

Class FlowRegimeDetector

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.pipeline.twophasepipe.FlowRegimeDetector
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class FlowRegimeDetector extends Object implements Serializable
Mechanistic flow regime detector based on Taitel-Dukler and Barnea models.

Determines the flow pattern in two-phase pipe flow based on local conditions including fluid properties, velocities, pipe geometry and inclination.

Supports two detection methods:

  • MECHANISTIC: Uses Taitel-Dukler (1976) and Barnea (1987) transition criteria
  • MINIMUM_SLIP: Selects flow regime with minimum slip ratio (closest to homogeneous)

References:

  • Taitel, Y. and Dukler, A.E. (1976) - A Model for Predicting Flow Regime Transitions in Horizontal and Near Horizontal Gas-Liquid Flow
  • Barnea, D. (1987) - A Unified Model for Predicting Flow-Pattern Transitions for the Whole Range of Pipe Inclinations

    • ANNULAR_BRIDGING_HOLDUP

      private static final double ANNULAR_BRIDGING_HOLDUP
      Liquid fraction above which the liquid can bridge the bore, so annular flow cannot be sustained.

      Barnea (1987) blockage criterion. A stable liquid slug needs a liquid fraction of about 0.48 in its body; bridging becomes possible once the film holds half of that, so annular flow requires an in-situ liquid fraction below 0.24.

    • setUseEquilibriumLevelAnnularTransition

      public void setUseEquilibriumLevelAnnularTransition(boolean enable)
      Select how the horizontal branch decides annular flow.

      The default path uses isAnnularFlow, which is the vertical droplet-entrainment criterion U_SG > 3.1 * (sigma * g * drho / rhoG^2)^0.25, and checks it ahead of the stratified/slug transition. In horizontal flow that threshold is small - about 1.6 m/s for a 200 mm gas line and 0.75 m/s for a 14-inch high-pressure export line - so it short-circuits the flow map and classifies effectively every gas pipeline as annular regardless of its liquid level, which then solves it with a thin-film closure.

      Enabling this selects the horizontal criterion of Taitel and Dukler (1976): after the Kelvin-Helmholtz instability has lifted the stratified layer, the branch is set by the equilibrium liquid level, annular below h_L/D = 0.5 and intermittent above it. Measured against a reference two-fluid simulator on a 73.8 km gas-condensate export line at 4 MSm3/d, this moves the holdup ratio from 0.84 to 1.02 on the median and from 0.83 to 0.96 on the mean, with pressure drop unchanged, and it correctly keeps the export line annular at 8.5 m/s while reclassifying a 200 mm line at 1.6 m/s as stratified-wavy and slug.

      This is the default. It was held back while the hold-up closures it routes to had no usable inclination response: on a 5 km 200 mm undulating fixture the equilibrium level itself swings from h_L/D = 0.058 on a 4 degree downhill section to 0.793 on a 4 degree uphill one, a factor of 47 in liquid area, while the hold-up returned for those same sections was 0.04303 and 0.04305, identical to five figures. Selecting the transition then replaced the annular film balance, the only closure carrying a gravity term, by closures that carried none, and the fixture's maximum-to-minimum hold-up ratio fell from 11.3 to 1.45 with the valley and peak ordering becoming arbitrary. Once the Taylor bubble film in the slug closure was given the same film balance the annular closure uses, that ratio returned to 11.6 with the valley above the peak, against 11.3 on the droplet path, so the two criteria now agree on the terrain response and differ only where they are meant to.

      The two paths differ only in the shallow-layer, sub-critical Kelvin-Helmholtz corner. On the export line above they return identical profiles at 10 MSm3/d, where the margin exceeds one in every section and both branch to annular; they differ at 4 MSm3/d, where the margin is below one in 85 per cent of sections. Disable this to recover the droplet-criterion behaviour.

      Parameters:
      enable - true to use the equilibrium-level transition

    • setBlendRegimeTransitions

      public void setBlendRegimeTransitions(boolean enable)
      Selects blending of the closures across horizontal regime transitions.

      Switching closure at a point steps hold-up and friction as an operating point drifts across a boundary, which shows up as a jump in pressure drop for a smooth change in terrain or rate. Blending ramps the weights over a band instead. Disable only to reproduce the hard-switching behaviour.

      Parameters:
      enable - true to blend across transitions

    • setUseMinimumSlipCriterion

      public void setUseMinimumSlipCriterion(boolean useMinimumSlip)
      Enable or disable minimum slip criterion for flow regime detection.

      When enabled, the detector calculates the slip ratio for each feasible flow regime and selects the one with minimum slip (closest to 1). This approach assumes the physical system naturally tends toward the flow pattern with minimum phase velocity difference.

      Parameters:
      useMinimumSlip - true to use minimum slip criterion, false for mechanistic approach

    • detectFlowRegime

      public PipeSection.FlowRegime detectFlowRegime(PipeSection section)
      Detect flow regime for a pipe section.

      Uses conservative phase holdups for single-phase detection. This keeps any positive phase inventory in the two-phase regime path even when its superficial velocity is arbitrarily small.

      Parameters:
      section - The pipe section with current state
      Returns:
      Detected flow regime

    • classify

      public PipeSection.FlowRegime classify(PipeSection section)
      Classifies a section, recording both the dominant regime and the transition blend.

      A section sitting on a regime boundary is not wholly one regime or the other. Hard switching there steps hold-up and friction discontinuously as an operating point drifts across the boundary. This sets the regime and, where the section is on a horizontal transition, the fractional weights the closures should be blended with.

      Parameters:
      section - section to classify; its regime and blend weights are updated
      Returns:
      the dominant flow regime

    • horizontalRegimeWeights

      private Map<PipeSection.FlowRegime,Double> horizontalRegimeWeights(PipeSection section, PipeSection.FlowRegime regime)
      Fractional regime weights across the horizontal stratified, annular and slug transitions.

      The stratified share follows the Kelvin-Helmholtz margin and the split of the remainder between annular and slug follows the equilibrium liquid level, both ramped over a band rather than switched at a point. Returns null when blending does not apply, in which case the single detected regime stands.

      Parameters:
      section - section being classified
      regime - the regime already detected for the section
      Returns:
      weights per regime, or null when a single regime applies

    • isWavyTransition

      private boolean isWavyTransition(double U_SL, double U_SG, double h_L, double D, double theta, double rho_L, double rho_G, double mu_L)
      Check transition from smooth to wavy stratified.

      Taitel and Dukler (1976) transition D, from Jeffreys' sheltering theory: waves grow when the gas can feed energy to the interface faster than viscous dissipation in the liquid removes it, U_G > sqrt(4 nu_L (rho_L - rho_G) g cos(theta) / (s rho_G U_L)). The group is a velocity squared only when the viscosity is kinematic and the divisor carries the liquid velocity; both were wrong here, which put the threshold near 52 m/s for air and water and left an ordinary wavy line reported as smooth.

      Parameters:
      U_SL - superficial liquid velocity, in m/s
      U_SG - superficial gas velocity, in m/s
      h_L - liquid height, in m
      D - pipe diameter, in m
      theta - inclination, in radians
      rho_L - liquid density, in kg/m3
      rho_G - gas density, in kg/m3
      mu_L - liquid dynamic viscosity, in Pa.s
      Returns:
      true if transition from smooth to wavy stratified occurs

    • bridgesTheBore

      private boolean bridgesTheBore(double h_L, double D)
      Whether the liquid at this level can bridge the bore, so annular flow cannot be sustained.

      Barnea (1987) blockage criterion, evaluated on the same stratified equilibrium level that transition B uses — the approximation already made there. Annular flow is impossible once the in-situ liquid fraction reaches 0.24. This is strictly stronger than the h_L/D < 0.5 level test, which corresponds to a liquid fraction of 0.5.

      Parameters:
      h_L - liquid height, in m
      D - pipe diameter, in m
      Returns:
      true when the liquid fraction is at or above the bridging limit
